A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same GenStereo research, and all 11 pages of each are readable, including equations, figures, tables, and references. Neither supplied PDF contains an appendix; both refer to supplementary visualizations outside the supplied documents.

before.justification: V1 reports original stereo-generation experiments, downstream stereo-matching evaluations, and component ablations in Tables 2–5.

after.justification: V2 retains those original experiments and adds results using SD v2.1 and IGEV++, alongside additional baseline results.

M1.justification: The coordinate conditioning, cross-view attention, losses, adaptive fusion, and disparity dropout remain unchanged. V2 clarifies CLIP image conditioning and evaluates additional model configurations, without establishing a change to the proposed procedure.

E1.justification: The eleven synthetic training datasets, five source datasets for generated matching data, and KITTI, Middlebury, and ETH3D evaluation coverage are retained. Added backbone configurations do not introduce new datasets or tasks.

E2.justification: Table 4 adds standalone PSMNet and RAFT-Stereo comparator rows, previously represented only as downstream architectures, and introduces an IGEV++ comparator. Existing generation and matching comparators remain.

E3.justification: V2 adds SD v2.1 configurations with reported 768 × 768 training crops and IGEV++ downstream evaluation. Existing splits, metrics, and three-epoch generator training remain. Table 5 also reverses the reported ground-truth/pseudo-disparity assignments, correcting a setting description without establishing that experiments were rerun.

E4.justification: The architecture-agnostic evaluation extends to IGEV++. Table 5 retains all eight component ablations and their scores but corrects their disparity-source labels: rows 1–2 use ground truth and rows 3–8 use pseudo disparities, rather than the reverse.

E5.justification: Table 2 retains the same asymmetric summary format and extends it to new rows without defining a new uncertainty procedure. Neither version specifies repeated-run counts, seeds, significance tests, or how these bounds are calculated.

E6.justification: Tables 2 and 4 substantially expand the numerical evidence with SD v2.1 results, standalone backbone baselines, and IGEV++ experiments. Newly reported SD v2.1 pseudo-disparity PSNR values are 25.142 on Middlebury and 23.488 on KITTI; GenStereo-trained IGEV++ reports KITTI 2012/2015 D1-all values of 2.802/3.746. All earlier numerical entries are retained, allowing for rounding in Table 4; these additions are new configurations, not same-setting improvements over v1.

T1.justification: Equations 1–11 retain the same coordinate mappings, attention construction, objectives, fusion rule, and dropout definitions. No new theoretical assumptions, propositions, or proofs appear.

C1.justification: The abstract removes the explicit claim that the framework eliminates the need for complex hardware setups. The principal novelty, generalization, and state-of-the-art generation and matching claims remain unchanged.

C2.justification: Section 4.1 removes the paragraph arguing that single-camera dataset construction expands applicability where dual-camera systems are impractical or costly. Interpretations of the component ablations and the limitation concerning large disparities remain unchanged.

D1.justification: Section 3.2 newly explains replacement of text conditioning with CLIP image embeddings, and Figure 2 identifies frozen and fine-tuned components. Tables 3 and 5 explicitly identify SD v1.5. The printed project address already existed as v1's hyperlink, so it does not establish a new resource release.

R1.justification: V2 adds citations for PSMNet, RAFT-Stereo, IGEV++, and the original Depth Anything paper. Related-work arguments remain essentially unchanged; several other bibliography changes update publication metadata for already cited works.

P1.justification: V2 removes 'GenStereo:' from the title, shortens the abstract and application discussion, adds implementation sentences and acknowledgments, and makes small editorial corrections. The section sequence and most prose remain unchanged.

P2.justification: Figure 2 adds embedding blocks and frozen/fine-tuned annotations. Table 2 gains an SD-version column, Table 4 gains rows and an IGEV++ group, and Table 5 corrects source labels. Figures 1 and 3 retain identical images, although Figure 3 and several tables move within the layout.

improvement.justification: V2 corrects Table 5's disparity-source labels to agree with Table 2 and the dropout discussion, clarifies implementation through Section 3.2 and Figure 2, and strengthens evaluation with additional architectures and standalone baselines. These are useful, bounded gains. The added configurations show mixed performance, while their training details and statistical reporting remain limited, so the revision does not establish a substantial overall quality improvement.
